title: Groups that carry policy
desc: Staffing a group, giving it a role, and narrowing which model tiers a team may use.
learningGoal: After this lesson you can build a group that carries the right role, model tiers and capability grants for one team, define a tier of your organisation's own, and predict what each of those does to a person who is in two groups at once.

steps.title: A group is a policy, not a mailing list
steps.bodyMd:
Van Dijk Groep has sixty people and one administrator. Setting the same five things on sixty rows, one at a time, is how organisations end up with access nobody can explain.

A group in Bee Flow is a named set of people **plus** the policy attached to them:

- a **Group Role** every member also acts as
- an **Allowed tiers** list — which AI model tiers members may pick
- the integrations and features granted to that team
- which agent types its members reach

The empty state says it plainly: *"Groups let you organise users and control which agents they can access."* Change the group once, and everyone in it moves together.

steps.title: Create it, then staff it
steps.bodyMd:
Settings → Organisation → **Users & Groups** → tab **Groups**.

Click **Create New Group**, fill in **Group name** (`Inkoop`) and **Description (optional)**, then **Create**. The card appears with *0 members*.

Two things worth knowing before you type the name:

- The name becomes the group's internal id, lower-cased with anything that is not a letter or number turned into a hyphen. Reuse a name and you get *"Group already exists"*.
- People you invite land in the organisation's **default groups** automatically, so day-one access is a property of the group rather than something an admin has to remember.

To staff it: expand the card, click **Add member**, and type in **Search users to add…** — the list shows the first twenty matches. You can also work from the other side: the person-plus button on someone's row on the **Users** tab (**Assign groups**) ticks several groups at once.

steps.title: Put the Inkoop group together
steps.instruction: Sanne, Joost and Bilal handle supplier quotations at Van Dijk Groep. Drag these five moves into the order you actually perform them.

items.label: Click Create New Group and fill in Group name and Description
Click Create — the card appears with 0 members
Expand the card, click Add member and search for each colleague

sim.feedback: The group has to exist before anyone can be put in it — Add member only appears on an expanded, saved group card. Everything that comes after (Group Role, Allowed tiers, integration grants) is edited on that same expanded card.

steps.title: One role for the whole team
steps.bodyMd:
Expand a group and you get **GROUP SETTINGS**. The **Group Role** dropdown starts at **User (default)** and then lists the six organisation roles: Organisation Admin, Data Protection Officer, ISMS Internal Auditor, Agent Admin, Agent Editor, Member.

Pick one and a hint appears: *"All members inherit this role"*. That is a fan-out, not a transfer. Everyone in the group now **also** acts as that role, on top of whatever role their own row carries.

Use it when a whole team needs the same standing — "everyone in Support may build agents" — instead of editing six rows and forgetting the seventh. Remove someone from the group and the inherited role goes with them; their personal role on the Users tab is untouched.

steps.question: Sanne's own role is Member. You set the Inkoop group's Group Role to Agent Editor. What may Sanne do now?

choices.label: Everything Member allows plus everything Agent Editor allows — the two are added together.
Only what Agent Editor allows; her Member role is replaced while she is in the group.
choices.feedback: Nothing is replaced. Her own role and every group role she holds are merged into one permission set. A group role is a shortcut for "everyone here also acts as this role", never a swap.

choices.label: Nothing yet — you still have to change her role on her own row in the Users tab.
choices.feedback: No second edit is needed. The group role reaches every member the moment you save it, and stops reaching them the moment they leave the group.

choices.label: Agent Editor things only inside the Inkoop group's own workspace.
choices.feedback: A group is not a workspace — there is no "inside" for permissions to be scoped to. What a group grants applies to that person everywhere in the organisation.

steps.explanation: Roles add up. A person's effective permissions are the union of their own role, every group role they inherit, and anything granted to their groups directly — which is why a group role is the cheapest way to give a whole team the same standing, and why you check group membership before you wonder how someone got a permission.

steps.title: Allowed tiers: narrowing the model menu
steps.bodyMd:
A **tier** is the class of AI model a person can choose for a task. Under **Allowed tiers** the group card shows a pill per tier — **Fast**, **Thinking**, **Writer**, **Deep Thinking**, plus any custom tiers your organisation has defined (you will build one in a moment).

Those are the admin-side spellings of the tiers your colleagues already know from chat, so line them up before you restrict anything: **Thinking** here is the depth slider's **Think**, and **Writer** here is the **Write** pill that sits *beside* the slider, not on it. The chat slider runs **Auto → Fast → Think → Deep Thinking**; Write is a kind of work (long-form), never a rung between Think and Deep Thinking. Clicking **Writer** off removes a kind of work, it does not lower a ceiling.

By default no pill is active and the hint reads: *"No restriction set — members can use every tier. Click a pill to restrict access to only selected tiers."*

Quote comparison at Van Dijk Groep is cheap, high-volume work, so the office manager clicks **Fast**. The hint changes to *"1 tier permitted…"* and the Inkoop team's model picker narrows to match.

It is reversible in one click: the **Clear restrictions** link puts the group back to no restriction. Nothing is deleted and nobody is logged out.

steps.question: Sanne has taken the everyday courses. She asks why the group card says Thinking and Writer when her chat shows Think on the slider and Write as a pill beside it. What do you tell her?

choices.label: Same tiers, two spellings: Thinking is chat's Think, Writer is chat's Write pill — and Write is a kind of work beside the slider, not a step above Think.
Writer is a heavier tier than Thinking that only admins can hand out, so it sits between Think and Deep Thinking.
choices.feedback: There is no rung between Think and Deep Thinking. The chat depth slider is Auto, Fast, Think, Deep Thinking; Write, like Flow and Swarm, renders as a pill beside it because it names a kind of work — long-form content — not an amount of effort.

choices.label: The group card lists model names while chat lists tiers, which is why the two never match.
choices.feedback: Neither screen names a model. Bee Flow asks how deep an answer should go, not which model to run; both the group pills and the chat slider are naming the same tiers.

choices.label: The card is incomplete — Auto is missing from the pills, so tier restrictions cannot be trusted.
choices.feedback: Nothing is missing. The Allowed tiers pills are Fast, Thinking, Writer and Deep Thinking plus any custom tiers your organisation defined; Auto is not one of them because Auto is the router choosing one of the others for you.

steps.explanation: One control set, two vocabularies: the admin card spells the tiers Fast, Thinking, Writer, Deep Thinking, and chat shows Fast, Think and Deep Thinking on the depth slider with Write as a pill beside it. When a colleague reports that an option vanished, translate their word into the pill name before you go looking.

steps.title: Where the custom pills come from
steps.bodyMd:
"Plus any custom tiers" is easy to read past. A custom tier is one your organisation defines itself: your own name, your own model behind it.

You build them on **Organisation Custom Tiers** — *"Create tiers scoped to this organisation. They appear alongside global tiers for your members."* Be warned: this panel has **no tab button** in Users & Groups. It opens only by typing the sub-page `customTiers` onto the Users & Groups address in the browser bar (`/app/org-settings/users/customTiers`). Bookmark it once and you never hunt for it again.

**+ Add Tier** drops in *New tier 1*. Give it an icon and a tier name — the name becomes the id, lower-cased as `custom:<name>` — a **Short description (shown in tier picker)**, a **Model**, an optional **EU override**, and the **Available for** pills **Direct Chat** and **Agent Chat**. Expand the row for **Max Tokens** (16384 by default) and **Temperature**. Then **Save Organisation Tiers**.

Van Dijk Groep's office manager makes one called *Offerte-check*, pinned to a small EU-hosted model and available for **Direct Chat** only. Underneath sits a **Global tiers (read-only)** block — those come from the system administrator and you cannot edit them here. Deleting your own asks first: *"Delete this custom tier? This cannot be undone."*

steps.question: Offerte-check is saved and shows up as a pill. But the Inkoop group was restricted to Fast last week, and Sanne still cannot pick the new tier. Why?

choices.label: A restricted group permits only the pills that are switched on, and Offerte-check is a pill like any other — click it on for Inkoop, or use Clear restrictions.
Custom tiers belong to the organisation, so they reach every member regardless of what a group restricts.
choices.feedback: Being organisation-scoped decides who may be shown the tier, not who is permitted it. Once a group's Allowed tiers list has anything selected, that list is the whole menu — your custom pill sits in it beside Fast, Thinking, Writer and Deep Thinking and has to be selected too.

choices.label: The tier has to be moved into the Global tiers block at the bottom of the panel before groups can see it.
choices.feedback: That block is labelled "Global tiers (read-only)" — it lists the tiers the system administrator provides and nothing can be moved into it from here. Your organisation's tiers live in the list above it.

choices.label: The tier still has to be granted to the Inkoop group on the Integration access tab.
choices.feedback: Integration access grants integrations, never tiers. A tier reaches a person through the Allowed tiers pills on their groups, and nowhere else.

steps.explanation: A custom tier changes what is on the menu; Allowed tiers still decides who may order from it. So every time you add one, walk the groups you have already restricted — an empty list widens by itself, but a restricted list never does.

steps.title: The widest group wins
steps.bodyMd:
This is the part that surprises administrators. Bee Flow asks one question per tier: *does at least one of this person's groups permit it?* Three consequences follow.

- **Two groups, two lists — you get the union.** Joost in Inkoop (Fast only) and in Sales (Thinking, Deep Thinking) may use all three.
- **An unrestricted group re-opens everything.** A group with an empty list permits every tier, so adding a restricted person to it removes the restriction in practice.
- **Someone in no group at all is unrestricted.** Restriction only exists through membership.

The screen warns you itself: *"Members of other groups may still see additional tiers through those groups."* To hold a team to one tier, every group those people belong to has to carry the same restriction.

steps.question: Joost is in Inkoop (Allowed tiers: Fast) and in Sales (no restriction set). Which tiers can he pick?

choices.label: All of them — a tier is allowed if any one of his groups permits it, and Sales permits everything.
Only Fast — the narrowest restriction across his groups wins.
choices.feedback: There is no narrowest-wins rule. The check is "does at least one of my groups permit this tier", so the widest group decides. Narrowing Inkoop while Sales stays open changes nothing for Joost.

choices.label: None — the two lists contradict each other, so his tier picker comes up empty.
choices.feedback: Conflicting lists never lock anyone out. An empty Allowed tiers list means "no restriction", not "nothing allowed" — the picker can only get wider, never empty.

choices.label: Fast, plus whatever his personal tier setting allows on his own row.
choices.feedback: There is no per-person tier setting anywhere in Users & Groups. Tiers are restricted through groups only, which is exactly why a second group can undo the first.

steps.explanation: Allowed tiers restricts one group, not one person. Before you promise anyone that a team cannot reach Deep Thinking, open each member's row and check every group they are in — the hint under the pills says the same thing in one line.

steps.title: Five requests, five instruments
steps.instruction: Van Dijk Groep has five requests this week. Match each one to the control that actually does the job — one of them is deliberately not a group setting at all.

pairs.left: Inkoop compares supplier quotes all day; the director does not want that work reaching the heaviest models.
pairs.note: A tier restriction on the group is the control that narrows the model picker for a team — and it only holds if Inkoop is the team's only group.

pairs.left: All six people in Support need to build and edit agents, and two more join next month.
pairs.note: Set it once on the group and next month's joiners inherit it the moment they are added — no per-person edit.

pairs.left: Sales needs the SignRequest e-signature integration; nobody else in the organisation should get it.
pairs.right: A group grant on Settings → Organisation → Integrations → Integration access
pairs.note: Integrations are granted per scope. Grant it to the Sales group rather than to All members, or everyone gets it.

pairs.left: The office manager must be able to open Compliance without being able to manage users.
pairs.right: A personal role on her own row: Data Protection Officer
pairs.note: This one is a personal role rather than a group. The Data Protection Officer role carries exactly two things — the Compliance Center and Usage & Monitoring — and no user management.

pairs.left: A new colleague starts on the 1st and should land in the right teams without anyone remembering to do it.
pairs.note: Invited joiners are placed into the organisation's default groups on arrival, so onboarding access is configuration rather than a checklist.

steps.title: Granting a tool is not adding a member
steps.bodyMd:
Integrations are handed out in Settings → Organisation → **Integrations** → **Integration access** — the tab that screen opens on. Pick a scope on the left — **All members**, or one group — then flip the toggles; saving is immediate.

The rule is simple: someone gets an integration if it is granted to All members **or** to any group they belong to. Pick a group and the screen says so — *"grants stack on top of All members"* — and anything already granted to everyone appears on the group's card marked *"Granted to all members"*, switched on and not clickable. Only what your subscription includes is listed here at all.

So there are two different actions on the same group: putting people in it, and granting it things. Adding Bilal to Sales gives him everything Sales has been granted — which is usually what you want, and occasionally exactly what you did not intend.

steps.question: The Gamma integration is granted to the Inkoop group and also to All members. You want Bilal to lose it. What actually works?

choices.label: Nothing at group level — the All members grant reaches everyone, so it has to be switched off there.
Remove Bilal from the Inkoop group.
choices.feedback: That removes only the Inkoop route. He still has it through All members, because a capability arrives if it is granted to All members or to any group he is in.

choices.label: Add Bilal to a group that has the integration toggled off.
choices.feedback: A group with the toggle off grants nothing; it does not deny anything. There is no deny switch in the access matrix, so putting someone in another group can never take an integration away from them.

choices.label: Clear the Inkoop group's Allowed tiers so the integration is no longer permitted.
choices.feedback: Allowed tiers governs which AI model tiers members may pick, nothing else. Integrations live on the Integration access tab — two separate controls that never talk to each other.

steps.explanation: Grant-only is the whole model: access is the union of every route a person has, so you remove access by removing routes, starting with the widest one. When the widest route is All members, narrowing a group achieves nothing — which is the argument for keeping the All members column deliberately thin.

steps.title: Build one real group and staff it
steps.instruction: In Users & Groups → Groups, click Create New Group, give it a real team name and description, and click Create. Expand the card and use Add member to put at least one colleague (or yourself) in it. Optionally set a Group Role or click an Allowed tiers pill — both are reversible.

steps.title: Synced groups are Managed, and they push back
steps.bodyMd:
If your organisation syncs groups from Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), those groups arrive on the same Groups tab with an **Azure AD** chip, a *Last synced* timestamp, and the word **Managed** where the delete button would be.

Split them in your head:

- **Membership belongs to the directory.** Someone you add by hand can be removed again by the next sync, and with **Destructive sync** switched on, memberships the directory no longer lists are cleared here too.
- **Policy stays yours.** A sync writes only the group's name, description and *Last synced* time — the **Group Role**, **Allowed tiers** and capability grants you set survive it.

So it is safe to hang policy on a synced group. It is not safe to hang membership on one.

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
- **Build a team group and staff it** — Groups tab, **Create New Group**, then **Add member** on the expanded card, or **Assign groups** from a person's row.
- **Attach policy instead of repeating it** — a **Group Role** that every member inherits, an **Allowed tiers** list that narrows the model picker — including any pill you added yourself on **Organisation Custom Tiers**, the panel that opens only via the `customTiers` address — and integration grants made per group on Settings → Organisation → Integrations → **Integration access**.
- **Predict the outcome for someone in two groups** — roles, grants and tiers all add up, so the widest group decides and nothing a group carries can ever subtract. Check every group a person is in before promising a limit.

Everything here is reversible: **Clear restrictions**, **User (default)** and an untoggled grant put a group straight back.

practiceTopic.title: Groups, group roles and allowed tiers
practiceTopic.summary: How a group in Users & Groups carries a role, a model-tier restriction and capability grants, and how those combine for someone in more than one group.
facts: Groups live in Settings → Organisation → Users & Groups, on the Groups tab, and are created with the Create New Group button; a name clash returns "Group already exists".
The Group Role dropdown starts at "User (default)" and shows the hint "All members inherit this role"; the role is added to, never swapped for, the person's own role.

Allowed tiers offers the pills Fast, Thinking, Writer and Deep Thinking plus any custom tiers — the admin names for chat's Fast/Think/Deep Thinking slider plus the Write pill beside it; an empty list means "No restriction set".
A tier is permitted if at least one of the person's groups permits it, so an unrestricted group widens everyone in it; the Clear restrictions link returns a group to no restriction in one click.
Organisation Custom Tiers has no tab button: it opens only via the customTiers sub-page of the Users & Groups address (/app/org-settings/users/customTiers).

On that panel + Add Tier creates "New tier 1"; a tier takes an icon, a name (which becomes the id custom:<name>), a short description shown in the tier picker, a Model, an optional EU override and the Available for pills Direct Chat and Agent Chat.
Expanding a custom tier reveals Max Tokens (16384 by default) and Temperature; Save Organisation Tiers commits them, and the Global tiers (read-only) block below comes from the system administrator.

Integrations are granted per scope on Settings → Organisation → Integrations → Integration access: someone gets one if it is granted to All members or to any of their groups — grants stack and never subtract.

actionChecks.label: Create and staff a group
actionChecks.hint: In Settings → Organisation → Users & Groups → Groups, use Create New Group, then Add member on the expanded card.

endpoints.returns: array of group rows for the caller's organisation, each with id, name, description, userCount, source, orgRole, allowedTiers

criteria.label: A group of your own exists
criteria.hint: Click Create New Group on the Groups tab and give it a team name.
criteria.rule: at least one row where id is neither 'admins' nor 'users' and source !== 'azure'

criteria.label: That group has at least one member
criteria.hint: Expand the group card, click Add member and pick a colleague (or yourself).
